section: Can reduced blood flow injure the nerve endings? > Flow is the delivery; oxygen is the thing delivered > What happened when someone measured oxygen at the nerve itself
sentence_as_it_stands: I do not have the full paper to resolve this, only the abstract, so I cannot tell whether that sentence is describing a different comparison than the one the table shows, or is simply an error in the abstract’s wording. What I am confident of is which of the two accounts the numbers and the stated conclusion agree with, and it is the reassuring one: oxygenation with epinephrine tracked saline, not bupivacaine.
quote: However, two nerves of the BupiEpi group did have relevant desaturations during measurements (SO2 nadir values of 3% at T20 and 10% at T10 in another nerve). Thus, despite no significant difference between both groups of bupivacaine, with and without epinephrine, we would recommend not to use epinephrine in a patient population with preexisting peripheral nerve damage (i.e., diabetic polyneuropathy).
corrected_wording: The full paper resolves the abstract's sentence. In the epinephrine group oxygen saturation fell early: its median was the lowest of the four groups from 5 to 30 minutes and was back at the saline level at 60 minutes, and two of its ten nerves desaturated severely. At 30 and 60 minutes the epinephrine group did not differ significantly from bupivacaine alone. Oxygenation with epinephrine matched saline at one hour, not during the first half hour, and the authors' discussion names patients with pre-existing peripheral nerve damage, such as diabetic polyneuropathy, as a group in whom they would not use epinephrine.
notes: Table 3 (PDF page 6, read from the rendered page) gives the time course of median SO2: epinephrine group 92.5 at baseline, 83.5 at 5 min, 74 at 10 min, about 83-86 from 15 to 30 min, 87 at 40, 90 at 50, 91 at 60; bupivacaine alone about 90-92 to 25 min, 89 at 30, then 84.5, 79.5, 76; saline 88.5-92 throughout. Tests were made only at 0, 30 and 60 min. The same 60-minute reading recurs in the next paragraph ('The anesthetic, not the epinephrine, is what lowered oxygenation: bupivacaine alone gave the worst reading of the four, at 76 percent' — true at 60 min only), in 'What this section does and does not establish' ('oxygen did not fall on average — with the qualification that the spread in that group included nerves which did', which is partly qualified already), in The verdict (F02) and in Sources (F05). The page reads the whole result as reassurance for a reader with a neuropathy; the authors' own caution for pre-existing nerve damage is not mentioned. Wiesmann used an epinephrine concentration higher than the page's, with bupivacaine, dripped on an exposed pig nerve (see F03). Page fetched whole (no truncation flags).

section: The verdict > What the literature got right
sentence_as_it_stands: … oxygen held up where it was measured at a nerve with flow halved; and a [dose figure omitted] wheal at [dose figure omitted] carries [dose figure omitted], [dose figure omitted] less than the smallest dose in any study quoted here. **Nothing here suggests harm was done.**
quote: Bupivacaine resulted in significant decrease in nerve blood flow, as well as tissue oximetry values, compared with saline control. Addition of epinephrine resulted in a rapid, but nonsignificant, reduction of nerve blood flow and extensive lowering of tissue oximetry levels.
corrected_wording: … where oxygen was measured at a nerve (pigs, bupivacaine dripped onto the exposed nerve), it fell: with bupivacaine alone it was significantly below saline at one hour, and with bupivacaine plus epinephrine, at a stronger epinephrine concentration than this page's, it fell during the first half hour, severely in two of ten nerves, before recovering by one hour; the authors judged that neither amounted to relevant ischaemia.
notes: Second place the overstatement of F01 appears, here in the verdict's list of what the literature got right, directly before 'Nothing here suggests harm was done.' Bupivacaine vs saline SO2 at 60 min: p = 0.0005 (Results, PDF page 5) and p = 0.003 (Table 5). The page elsewhere already notes the concentration is not the page's; this sentence does not.

section: Can reduced blood flow injure the nerve endings? > Flow is the delivery; oxygen is the thing delivered > What happened when someone measured oxygen at the nerve itself
sentence_as_it_stands: The concentration and volume Wiesmann’s group used are not given in the abstract, which is a real gap: it means the study establishes that flow can fall by more than half without oxygen following it down, but not at exactly what dose.
quote: Randomly, [dose figure omitted] of the following test solutions was applied topically to the nerve: bupivacaine [dose figure omitted] isobaric (Bupi) … with epinephrine [dose figure omitted] (BupiEpi) (Suprarenin, Sanofi-Aventis, Frankfurt, Germany)
corrected_wording: The full paper gives the concentration and volume ([dose figure omitted]): a single fixed volume of bupivacaine with epinephrine dripped onto the exposed nerve, at an epinephrine concentration higher than the one this page uses. So the study shows nerve blood flow falling by more than half with oxygen saturation back at the saline level one hour later, at a stronger epinephrine concentration than this page's and always together with bupivacaine; during the first half hour oxygen saturation in that group did fall.
notes: Answers the gap the page names. The concentration itself is stated only in the paper card and in C074's reason, per the brief. The adjacent sentence 'Blood flow with epinephrine fell to 41 percent of baseline — a large reduction, larger than anything measured in human skin at [dose figure omitted]' sets this stronger-concentration, bupivacaine-plus-epinephrine nerve result against skin data at the page's concentration; the page's own next paragraph already attributes most of the fall to bupivacaine (alone: a third of baseline).

section: Gaps in the literature: nobody has measured this > Disagreements between studies that are not resolved > What is held at second hand, and what that costs
sentence_as_it_stands: **Wiesmann 2018** — open access, but only the abstract was obtained, and the abstract omits the concentration and volume. The cost: the one study that measured flow and oxygen on the same nerve at the same time establishes that flow can halve without oxygen following, at an unknown dose. It also contains a sentence that contradicts its own table, and the full text is what would resolve which is right.
corrected_wording: Wiesmann 2018 has been read in full (it is free in PMC). It states the concentration and volume — the epinephrine concentration was higher than this page's — and it resolves the sentence: the 'extensive lowering of tissue oximetry' with epinephrine describes the first half hour, when that group's median oxygen saturation was the lowest of the four groups and two of its nerves desaturated severely, before it recovered to the saline level by one hour. Abstract and table agree once the time course is read.
notes: The quote is the 10-minute column of Table 3 (median SO2 with interquartile range) in the order bupivacaine, saline, bupivacaine-clonidine, bupivacaine-epinephrine; the epinephrine group's 74 is the lowest reading of any group before 40 min. The text file scrambles the rotated table; the column order was confirmed on the rendered page. The page names this as one of the gaps that would 'move' sentences if the full text arrived; the sentences that move are F01-F03 and F05.

section: Sources > Blood flow and oxygen at a nerve (Wiesmann entry)
sentence_as_it_stands: *Full abstract read via DOAJ, open access; full text not obtained.* — The one study measuring flow and oxygen on the same nerve at the same time: median flow 0.41 of baseline with epinephrine (IQR 0.30–0.54), oxygen saturation median 91 percent (IQR 56–92) against saline’s 91.5 (84–95). The paper’s stated conclusion and its own numbers agree that epinephrine did not significantly worsen oxygenation beyond bupivacaine alone; one sentence in the Results, describing an “extensive lowering of tissue oximetry” with epinephrine, does not match either. Limits: 40 pig nerves split four ways, ten per group; bupivacaine rather than lidocaine; concentration and volume not given in the abstract.
quote: Measurements of nerve blood flow (flow in arbitrary units [AU]), tissue oxygen saturation (SO2 in %), and tissue hemoglobin level (rHb, in AU) were obtained using laserDoppler flowmetry and tissue spectrophotometry (O2C; Lea Medizintechnik, Giessen, Germany).
corrected_wording: Full text read (free in PMC, PMC5789040); the author list is confirmed. The one study measuring flow and oxygen on the same nerve at the same time after a local anaesthetic or adjuvant (an earlier rat study measured both without any drug: Ibrahim 1999). Time course: in the epinephrine group oxygen saturation fell over the first half hour and recovered by one hour, and two of ten nerves desaturated severely; the 'extensive lowering of tissue oximetry' sentence describes that early phase. Limits: 40 pig median nerves exposed in the axilla, ten per group; bupivacaine rather than lidocaine; epinephrine at a stronger concentration than this page's, dripped onto the exposed nerve; one hour of recording; no histology.
notes: The 'extensive lowering' sentence is in the abstract's results, not a separate Results section. Ibrahim 1999 (PMID 10374827, Wiesmann reference 29; abstract cached) measured nerve oxygen saturation and perfusion together in healthy rat sciatic nerves, so 'the one study measuring flow and oxygen on the same nerve' holds only for studies with a local anaesthetic.

section: Lidocaine with epinephrine for intradermal wheals in small fiber neuropathy > The result
sentence_as_it_stands: The one study that measured blood flow *inside a nerve* found [dose figure omitted] to be the one strength at which epinephrine alone did not reduce it — a finding that weakens once lidocaine joins it (see "The one measurement of blood flow inside a nerve at exactly this concentration, and what changes once lidocaine is added").
quote: Combined tissue spectrophotometry and laser-Doppler flowmetry were used to assess nerve blood flow in 40 surgically exposed median nerves in pigs, as well as nerve tissue oximetry for 60 min.
corrected_wording: The one study that measured blood flow inside a nerve at this concentration (Partridge 1991) found it to be the one strength at which epinephrine alone did not reduce it — a finding that weakens once lidocaine joins it. The other nerve blood-flow studies with epinephrine (Myers 1989, Palmer 2002, Bouaziz 2005, Wiesmann 2018) used stronger concentrations.
notes: Ambiguous, so recorded as low: the sentence may mean 'the one study at this concentration', which is accurate (C074 stays confirmed); read literally it says only one study ever measured blood flow inside a nerve, which the page itself contradicts by discussing Myers, Palmer, Bouaziz and Wiesmann. Wiesmann's probe sampled about 1-2 mm deep inside the nerve (PDF page 2).

section: Why the finger and nerve-trunk figures do not transfer > The dissenting measurement
sentence_as_it_stands: That result contradicts Myers at the same concentration. The two differ in instrument and in route, and neither difference has been isolated.
quote: Lidocaine ([dose figure omitted]) and epinephrine ([dose figure omitted]) injected alone did not alter blood flow in sciatic nerve, perisciatic muscle, or masseter muscle.
corrected_wording: That result contradicts Myers, although Palmer's epinephrine concentration was higher than the one Myers used, which sharpens the disagreement rather than explaining it. The two also differ in instrument and in route, and none of the three differences has been isolated.
notes: Rests on two studies from Wiesmann's reference list (refs 4 and 22; abstracts cached as a_2817471 and a_12351299): Myers 1989 applied epinephrine at a lower concentration than Palmer 2002 injected. The page's own Myers table and its Palmer paragraph state the two different concentrations. A reading of 'the same concentration' as the lidocaine strength (1 percent was common to both) is possible but less natural, since the preceding sentences are about epinephrine. Wiesmann used the same epinephrine concentration as Palmer.
